candidates.title: Generation increment is permanently DoS'd: _incrementGeneration calls EntropyGenerator.initializeAlphaIndices() which is onlyOwner, but the caller is the NFT contract (not the owner)
candidates.description: EntropyGenerator.initializeAlphaIndices() is `public whenNotPaused onlyOwner`. It is invoked by TraitForgeNft._incrementGeneration() (line 353) on every generation rollover. The Ownable owner of EntropyGenerator is the deployer EOA, while the caller in that path is the TraitForgeNft contract -> the onlyOwner check reverts. Unless ownership of EntropyGenerator is transferred to the NFT contract (and the contract has no transferOwnership call site here), every generation rollover reverts, so once generation 1 fills (10000 mints) all further _mintInternal calls (which trigger _incrementGeneration) revert -> minting and forging into new generations are bricked. Core-protocol DoS.

candidates.title: Fully predictable entropy lets users selectively mint to obtain forger / high-value (golden) tokens
candidates.description: Entropy slots are filled deterministically: entropySlots[i] = keccak256(block.number, i) % 10**78, and getPublicEntropy(slotIndex, numberIndex) is a PUBLIC view exposing any slot's derived entropy. The consumption cursor (currentSlotIndex, currentNumberIndex) advances deterministically and is read off-chain, so a user can compute the EXACT entropy their next mint will receive before sending the tx. Entropy fully determines value-bearing traits: isForger (entropy%3==0, required to list for forging), forgePotential ((entropy/10)%10), nukeFactor (entropy/40 -> claimable share of NukeFund), performanceFactor. An attacker mints only when the upcoming entropy is favorable (or via a wrapper contract that reverts otherwise), cherry-picking forgers / high-nuke tokens and extracting value from honest minters. Mint price is identical regardless of entropy, so this is a pure unfair-advantage / fund-extraction vector.

candidates.title: NukeFund can be drained: nuke() pays a share proportional to entropy-derived nukeFactor independent of what the nuker paid, so minting cheap high-entropy tokens and nuking extracts more than deposited
candidates.description: nuke() computes potentialClaimAmount = fund * finalNukeFactor / MAX_DENOMINATOR with finalNukeFactor = initialNukeFactor(entropy/40) + age term; initialNukeFactor alone reaches ~25000 (entropy<1e6) => up to fund/4 per nuke (capped at fund/2). The claim is a function of the token's entropy/age, NOT of the mint price the nuker paid (0.005 ETH base). Because entropy is predictable (T-02), an attacker mints cheap tokens with high nukeFactor, waits minimumDaysHeld (3 days), and nukes to claim a large fraction of a fund built mostly from other users' mint fees -> net drain of honest participants' contributions. Combined with T-02 this is a profitable permissionless extraction.

candidates.title: mintWithBudget loop gates on global _tokenIds instead of per-generation count -> unusable after 10000 total mints, and ignores the per-generation cap
candidates.description: The loop condition is `while (budgetLeft >= mintPrice && _tokenIds < maxTokensPerGen)`. `_tokenIds` is the cumulative all-time token id counter, but maxTokensPerGen (10000) is a PER-GENERATION cap. Once 10000 tokens total have been minted (i.e. from generation 2 onward), `_tokenIds < maxTokensPerGen` is permanently false, so the loop body never executes: mintWithBudget refunds the entire msg.value and mints nothing, becoming permanently unusable. The correct guard is generationMintCounts[currentGeneration] < maxTokensPerGen (as used in _mintInternal/_mintNewEntity).

candidates.title: EntityForging.forgeWithListed does not refund msg.value in excess of the forging fee -> overpayment permanently locked in the contract
candidates.description: forgeWithListed requires msg.value >= forgingFee, then distributes exactly forgingFee (devFee + forgerShare). Any excess (msg.value - forgingFee) is neither refunded nor accounted -> it stays stuck in EntityForging with no withdrawal path. Users who overpay (e.g. because the lister front-runs a fee change, or simply round up) lose the excess.

candidates.title: Forge-count off-by-one lets an entity forge forgePotential+1 times
candidates.description: listForForging requires `forgingCounts[tokenId] <= forgePotential` (inclusive) and does not increment; forgeWithListed increments forgingCounts AFTER. Because the gate is `<=` rather than `<`, a forger with forgePotential = P can be re-listed while forgingCounts == P and forge once more, yielding P+1 forges. Minor accounting/over-forge beyond the intended cap.

candidates.title: DevFund reward precision: amountPerWeight = msg.value / totalDevWeight truncates; with large total weight, per-deposit rewards round to zero and the full deposit is siphoned to owner()
candidates.description: receive() computes amountPerWeight = msg.value / totalDevWeight and forwards the remainder (msg.value - amountPerWeight*totalDevWeight) to owner(). The dev-fee deposits from minting are small (~10% of a 0.005 ETH mint = 5e14 wei). If totalDevWeight is set on a large scale, amountPerWeight truncates toward 0 and most/all of each deposit is routed to owner() as 'remaining' rather than accruing to devs -> dev rewards are silently lost to the owner. Weight scaling is admin-set but the rounding is unbounded by design.

candidates.title: EntropyGenerator.writeEntropyBatch1/2/3 are public with no access control
candidates.description: The three batch-initialization functions that populate entropySlots are `public` with no onlyOwner/onlyAllowedCaller gate. Anyone can call them (and choose the block.number that seeds the deterministic values). While the values are deterministic regardless of caller, the missing access control combined with block.number-seeded generation lets an attacker grind the block at which initialization occurs to bias the entropy table they later predict/consume (reinforces T-02).

candidates.title: NukeFund nuke maturity resets on every transfer (lastTokenTransferredTimestamp), and listing on EntityTrading counts as a transfer
candidates.description: canTokenBeNuked uses block.timestamp - getTokenLastTransferredTimestamp(tokenId) >= minimumDaysHeld. Listing a token on EntityTrading transfers it to the marketplace contract (resetting the clock), and buying transfers again. This is mostly anti-flip by design, but note tokens bought on the secondary market always restart the 3-day clock, and a self-transfer is excluded (from==to) — a buyer cannot nuke a freshly-bought NFT for 3 days even if it was old. Behavioral / minor. Documented for completeness.
